title: Azzi Fudd becomes first rookie to win WNBA 3-point contest
content:
CHICAGO — No rookie had ever won the WNBA’s 3-point contest, but arguably no shooter had ever entered the league with as perfect a jumper as Azzi Fudd.

Dallas Wings general manager Curt Miller said before the contest that he was nervous for Fudd, but he had no reason to be.

Fudd won the 3-point contest with 31 points in the final round, recording the second-highest score in contest history behind Sabrina Ionescu’s 37 in 2023.

The No. 1 draft pick out of UConn made 17-of-27 jumpers in the first round to advance with a score of 24, but she heated up in the final, knowing she would need a better effort to beat Portland’s Bridget Carleton, who led the first round with 29 points. Fudd made her first seven 3s in a row, nearly swept her money ball rack, and finished off four consecutive jumpers. She finished with 21 makes.

Carleton had to follow Fudd, but missed her first three looks and then four in a row on the middle rack, eliminating her from contention.

The crowd was loudly behind Fudd, especially as she started the final round with a flurry. Former UConn teammate KK Arnold was up on the baseline after every shot alongside incoming Husky Kelis Fisher. Fellow current and former Huskies Sarah Strong and Kaitlyn Chen were also courtside. Dallas forward Alysha Clark was wearing Fudd’s jersey.

Elena Delle Donne played her last WNBA game in Sept. 2023, but her jump shot looks like it hasn’t taken a day off since.

In the inaugural WNBA All-Star Shooting Stars Challenge, Team Washington — made up of Delle Donne, current Mystic Shakira Austin and high school player Jezelle “GG” Banks — took the win in large part because its legend was in the best form of any of the four former WNBA players. While the rest of the retired players struggled to hit from the long range, the first 50-40-90 player in WNBA history found her stroke from distance to help Washington advance to the final round, and then the youngster took it home.

Banks, a gold medalist for the USA at the U-18 level and a member of Team Durant in grassroots basketball, hit three of the six jumpers in the first round before finishing with two half-court shots (no other team hit more than one). She carried the team in the final round, when they knew they had to hit a target score of 25. She made more of the first six jumpers and hit the half-court shot to give Washington 27 points.

Washington kept shooting even after they had the trophy secured, and Banks made another halfcourt shot, earning the largest cheers of the evening as she celebrated the victory.

As Delle Donne told the broadcast following the competition, her stamina wasn’t there for the second round, and she needed Banks to carry the load. The Class of 2027 recruit is ranked No. 4 nationally by the 247Sports Composite.

The winner of the Shooting Stars competition gets $15,000 from the WNBA and an additional $85,000 from Aflac through a partnership with the WNBPA. Every current player participant makes $7,500 for appearing.
